# kodokan

Study Kodokan Judo throws from video via body-pose analysis: download technique
demonstrations, extract two-person (tori/uke) skeletons, split each clip into its
repeated demonstrations, visualize them, and compare/score demonstrations.

```python
from kodokan.acquire import download_techniques
from kodokan.track import estimate_poses_tracked
from kodokan.segment import segment_demonstrations
from kodokan.viz import render_skeleton_video

res = download_techniques(playlist_items="2")[0]  # Seoi-nage (#002), with metadata
seq = estimate_poses_tracked(
    res.path, source_url=res.info["webpage_url"]
)  # tracked tori/uke COCO-17
demos = segment_demonstrations(
    seq, min_two_person_frac=0.3
)  # per-demo (start_s, end_s)
render_skeleton_video(
    seq, out_path="overlay.mp4", source_video=res.path
)  # skeletons on the video
render_skeleton_video(
    seq, out_path="skeleton.mp4", blank_canvas=True
)  # skeletons on blank canvas
```

## What it does

A functional pipeline over the official *Kodokan 100 Techniques* YouTube playlist:

```default
acquire (yb) ─► pose (rtmlib / YOLO, tracked tori/uke) ─► segment (motion-energy)
       └─► dol stores (Parquet pose + JSON segments) ─► visualize (overlay / blank / Rerun)
       └─► compare two demos (joint-angle DTW) ─► score + eval harness
```

YouTube acquisition lives in the [`yb`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/yb) package
(`download_youtube_playlist`); `kodokan` is the analysis layer on top.

## Install

`import kodokan` needs only **numpy**; everything heavy is an optional extra (imported
lazily on first use), so the import never fails for a missing one:

```bash
pip install -e '.[all]'      # or pick extras: .[pose,track,viz,analysis,storage,acquire]
```

| extra      | for                                                 | brings                                                     | licence               |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| `pose`     | pose estimation (RTMPose, the default backend)      | rtmlib, onnxruntime                                        | permissive            |
| `track`    | stable tori/uke identity (`estimate_poses_tracked`) | ultralytics (+ `ultralytics-thop`, `ultralytics-platform`) | **AGPL-3.0-or-later** |
| `viz`      | rendering                                           | opencv-python, rerun-sdk, supervision, matplotlib          | permissive            |
| `analysis` | segment / compare / score                           | scipy, dtaidistance, pandas, pyarrow                       | permissive            |
| `storage`  | dol stores                                          | dol                                                        | permissive            |
| `acquire`  | YouTube download                                    | yb                                                         | permissive            |

`track` is separated from `pose` on purpose — see
[Licensing of extras](). The example at the top of this README
uses `estimate_poses_tracked`, so it needs `track`; `estimate_poses` alone does not.

You also need **ffmpeg** on PATH (acquisition/merge). The optional **3D lift**
(`scripts/lift_3d_mediapipe.py`) runs in a **separate venv**, because MediaPipe is
ABI-incompatible with numpy 2.x:

```bash
python -m venv ~/.kodokan_mp
~/.kodokan_mp/bin/pip install 'mediapipe==0.10.18' 'numpy<2' 'opencv-python-headless==4.10.0.84'
```

Data (videos, keypoints, renders, weights) lives **outside the repo** under
`~/kodokan_data` (override with `KODOKAN_DATA_DIR`).

## Licensing of extras

kodokan itself is **MIT**, and `pip install kodokan` installs **numpy and nothing
else** — no copyleft reaches you through the core package.

One extra is different, and it is worth reading before you type it:

> **`kodokan[track]` installs [ultralytics](https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics),
> which is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later.** `kodokan[all]` includes it too.

It is three distributions, not one — ultralytics pulls two more of its own, and both
carry the same licence, so listing only the first would understate what lands in your
environment:

| distribution           | licence           | how it arrives                               |
|------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `ultralytics`          | AGPL-3.0-or-later | declared by the `track` extra                |
| `ultralytics-thop`     | AGPL-3.0-or-later | hard dependency of `ultralytics`             |
| `ultralytics-platform` | AGPL-3.0-only     | dependency of `ultralytics` on Python ≥ 3.11 |

kodokan imports only the first; the other two arrive with it and are covered by the
same adjudication.

The AGPL is not “the GPL but for Python”. Its section 13 adds a **network clause**:
if you modify the work and let users interact with it *over a network*, those users
are entitled to the complete corresponding source of the whole combined work — even
though you never distributed a copy to anyone. Deploying a judo-analysis service
built on `kodokan[track]` is exactly that situation. The obligation attaches to the
combined work, not to ultralytics alone. That is the conservative reading — the one
this project plans around — rather than settled case law, but “we only import it” is
not a position worth betting a product on.

If that is not compatible with what you are building, you have two options:

1. **Do not install `track`.** Everything below still works.
2. **Buy an [Ultralytics Enterprise License](https://www.ultralytics.com/license)**,
   which Ultralytics sells precisely for commercial use that cannot accept the AGPL.

**What you can do without it.** Everything except identity tracking:

- `estimate_poses(...)` — the default `backend="rtmlib"` (RTMPose over onnxruntime)
  is AGPL-free and is what `kodokan[pose]` installs. It keeps the two
  highest-confidence people per frame, ordered left→right *per frame*.
- `segment`, `compare`, `score`, `store`, `viz`, `acquire` — all permissive.

**What you give up.** `kodokan.track.estimate_poses_tracked` runs Ultralytics’
built-in BoT-SORT/ByteTrack so tori and uke keep persistent identities across a
clip instead of swapping whenever they cross. rtmlib is a pose estimator with no
multi-object tracker, so this is a real feature difference, not a packaging one.
`estimate_poses(backend="ultralytics")` — the non-default YOLO11-pose backend —
also needs it. Both raise an `ImportError` naming the extra and the licence rather
than a bare `ModuleNotFoundError`.

The decision to keep this dependency, and the conditions that should reopen it,
are recorded in `[tool.wads.licence]` in `pyproject.toml`.

## The pipeline

| module                | purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `kodokan.acquire`     | download techniques (wraps `yb`), skip the PV, keep source URLs                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `kodokan.pose`        | `estimate_poses` facade (rtmlib / ultralytics backends), COCO-17, `PoseSequence`                                                                                                                                                |
| `kodokan.track`       | `estimate_poses_tracked` — stable tori/uke identity (BoT-SORT + spatial continuity)                                                                                                                                             |
| `kodokan.segment`     | hysteresis motion-energy segmentation + two-person gate + self-similarity                                                                                                                                                       |
| `kodokan.store`       | `pose_store` (tidy Parquet) / `segments_store` (JSON), the analysis SSOT                                                                                                                                                        |
| `kodokan.viz`         | overlay / blank-canvas MP4 + Rerun logging                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `kodokan.compare`     | joint-angle (soft-)DTW comparison of two demonstrations                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `kodokan.score`       | reference-based 0–100 scoring + per-joint/per-phase feedback                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `kodokan.descriptors` | experimental feature descriptors (for the eval harness)                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `kodokan.recognizer`  | `TechniqueRecognizer` (top-k guesses + every technique’s score), `recognize_segments` (a whole video), `ThrowDetector` / `LiveRecognizer` (rolling pose buffer, one guess per closed throw)                                     |
| `kodokan.coach`       | `coach` (0–100 + per-joint / per-phase deviation + EN/FR advice on the worst dimensions), `LiveCoach` (the same per detected throw on a live stream)                                                                            |
| `kodokan.testmode`    | `TechniqueTest` (random technique from a focus pool; graded on the recognizer’s confidence for it, plus closeness and advice when a reference is given), `LiveTechniqueTest` (the prompt, perform, grade loop on a live stream) |

Runnable end-to-end examples live in `examples/` (`warmup_seoinage.py`,
`batch_pipeline.py`, `segment_review.py`, `compare_demos.py`, `score_demos.py`,
`eval_features.py`).

## Dataset

`examples/batch_pipeline.py` builds a small dataset (10 techniques · 84
demonstrations · 18.3k frames) into the `dol` stores. Load it:

```python
from kodokan.store import pose_store, segments_store, load_all_tidy

seq = pose_store()["zIq0xI0ogxk"]  # (F, 2, 17, 3) COCO-17 (x, y, conf)
demos = segments_store()["zIq0xI0ogxk"]  # demo intervals + source_url
df = load_all_tidy()  # tidy DataFrame across all clips
```

See [`misc/docs/dataset.md`]().

## Status & honest limits

Works well: acquisition, tracked two-person pose, demo segmentation, the dol stores,
visualization, and same-technique demo comparison (joint-angle DTW is speed-invariant)
with interpretable per-joint/per-phase feedback.

Does **not** work yet — and this is *measured, not assumed*: **technique recognition /
cross-demo scoring**. A feature bake-off ([`misc/docs/feature-bakeoff.md`]())
shows every 2D descriptor *and* MediaPipe 3D joint angles sit at chance (separation
AUC ≈ 0.49–0.56). The blockers are noisy monocular 3D under grappling occlusion,
tori/uke role inconsistency, and the weakness of hand-crafted angle-DTW for few
examples — not viewpoint alone. Recognition needs a **learned** skeleton representation
(few-shot JEANIE, or trained PoseC3D/CTR-GCN) and/or cleaner multi-person 3D with
role-consistent features. The eval harness (`examples/eval_features*.py`) is ready to
validate those.

## Background & rationale

- [`misc/docs/research-architecture.md`]() — cited
  tools/architecture research (75 refs).
- [`misc/docs/dataset.md`]() — dataset card.
- [`misc/docs/feature-bakeoff.md`]() — why hand-crafted
  features don’t discriminate techniques (the empirical finding).

# _autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md

# kodokan.acquire

Acquire Kodokan technique clips from YouTube (thin wrapper over `yb.download`).

YouTube interaction lives in the `yb` package; this module just points it at the
kodokan data dir and the *Kodokan 100 Techniques* playlist, and keeps the source
URL with every clip (a project requirement). The PV (entry #1, “all techniques
once”) is skipped from the main line by default but can be fetched as a reference.

### Module Attributes

| [`KODOKAN_PLAYLIST_URL`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.KODOKAN_PLAYLIST_URL)   | The official "KODOKAN × IJF ACADEMY 100 Techniques" playlist.                         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SOURCES`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.SOURCES)                | Registered technique-demo sources (for cross-source / leave-one-clip-out validation). |

### Functions

| [`canonical_technique_key`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.canonical_technique_key)(title)                     | Normalize a clip title to a cross-source technique key.                            |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`download_source`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.download_source)(source, \*[, playlist_items, ...]) | Download a registered SOURCE playlist into its own clips dir.                      |
| [`download_techniques`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.download_techniques)(\*[, playlist_items, ...])     | Download technique clips into the kodokan clips dir (PV skipped by default).       |
| [`list_techniques`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.list_techniques)(\*[, include_pv])                  | List the playlist's videos (id, title, webpage_url, duration) without downloading. |
| [`local_clips`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.local_clips)([directory])                           | List already-downloaded clips on disk (decouples processing from download).        |
| [`source_clips_dir`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.source_clips_dir)(source)                           | Per-source clips directory (Kodokan keeps the legacy flat `clips/` dir).           |

### kodokan.acquire.KODOKAN_PLAYLIST_URL *= 'https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLtz539PTepc16H2iu5F3Q3D7_He1EYlIQ'*

The official “KODOKAN × IJF ACADEMY 100 Techniques” playlist.

### kodokan.acquire.SOURCES *= {'efficient_judo': 'https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLwd8pJWYTk07K6hDg2_N-9xd31gUCsew7', 'kodokan_ijf': 'https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLtz539PTepc16H2iu5F3Q3D7_He1EYlIQ'}*

Registered technique-demo sources (for cross-source / leave-one-clip-out validation).
Each is an *independent* set of demonstrations (different demonstrators/cameras), so the
SOURCE video can be used as the cross-validation group while `technique_key` is the label.

### kodokan.acquire.canonical_technique_key(title)

Normalize a clip title to a cross-source technique key.

Handles “kanji / Romaji” (Kodokan) and “Romaji - Demo” (Efficient Judo) titles,
the `-barai`/`-harai` spelling, and hyphen/space differences. E.g. both
“大外刈 / O-soto-gari” and “Osoto-gari - Demo” -> “osotogari”.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### kodokan.acquire.download_source(source, , playlist_items=None, download_dir=None, write_info_json=True, \*\*kwargs)

Download a registered SOURCE playlist into its own clips dir.

* **Parameters:**
  * **source** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a key of [`SOURCES`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.SOURCES) (e.g. `"efficient_judo"`).
  * **playlist_items** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – yt-dlp 1-based selector (default: all entries).
  * **download_dir** ([`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – override (default: [`source_clips_dir()`](_autosummary/kodokan.acquire.html.md#kodokan.acquire.source_clips_dir)).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – forwarded to `yb.download.download_youtube_playlist`.

### kodokan.acquire.download_techniques(, playlist_items=None, skip_pv=True, download_dir=None, write_info_json=True, \*\*kwargs)

Download technique clips into the kodokan clips dir (PV skipped by default).

* **Parameters:**
  * **playlist_items** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – yt-dlp 1-based selector (overrides `skip_pv`), e.g.
    `"2"` (only Seoi-nage), `"2:11"` (the first ten throws), `"2:"` (all).
  * **skip_pv** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – When `playlist_items` is not given, skip entry #1 (the PV).
  * **download_dir** ([`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Destination (default: [`kodokan.config.clips_dir()`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.clips_dir)).
  * **write_info_json** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Save each clip’s metadata sidecar (keeps the source URL).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Forwarded to `yb.download.download_youtube_playlist`.
* **Returns:**
  `list[yb.download.DownloadResult]` — media path + trimmed info + sidecars.

### kodokan.acquire.list_techniques(, include_pv=False, \*\*kwargs)

List the playlist’s videos (id, title, webpage_url, duration) without downloading.

* **Parameters:**
  * **include_pv** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Include entry #1 (the all-techniques PV) if True.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Forwarded to `yb.download.youtube_playlist_info`.

### kodokan.acquire.local_clips(directory=None)

List already-downloaded clips on disk (decouples processing from download).

Reads each `*.info.json` sidecar and pairs it with its `.mp4`. Returns
dicts with `id`, `title`, `webpage_url`, `path`. Sidecars without a
matching video (e.g. the playlist-level info.json) are skipped.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### kodokan.acquire.source_clips_dir(source)

Per-source clips directory (Kodokan keeps the legacy flat `clips/` dir).

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)


# _autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md

# kodokan.canon3d

Pelvis-frame (Procrustes) canonicalization of 3D world landmarks.

The Stage-5  *“3D refutes viewpoint”* conclusion was **withdrawn** by the
adversarial review (`misc/docs/adversarial-review.md`): MediaPipe per-crop
world landmarks are camera-aligned — not canonicalized — and the bounding-box
crop distorts their scale/orientation, so 3D joint angles computed straight off
them are **not** actually viewpoint-invariant. Before a fair 2D-vs-3D test, each
frame’s landmarks must be expressed in a *subject-centered anatomical frame*:
origin at the pelvis, axes fixed to the body (hip line + spine), scale normalized
by torso length. This module provides that canonicalization as a pure, testable
geometric function.

After [`canonicalize_pose()`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.canonicalize_pose), two demonstrations of the same articulated pose
seen from different camera azimuths map to the **same** canonical coordinates
(invariant to camera rotation, translation, and — with `scale=True` — subject
size). Downstream angle/position features are then genuinely viewpoint-invariant.

Indices default to the MediaPipe **BlazePose-33** convention used by the repo’s
3D lift (`scripts/lift_3d_mediapipe.py`); pass `joints=COCO17` (or a custom
[`BodyJoints`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.BodyJoints)) to reuse it for any layout exposing both hips and shoulders.

### Module Attributes

| [`BLAZEPOSE33`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.BLAZEPOSE33)   | MediaPipe BlazePose-33 (the repo's 3D-lift output format).                   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`COCO17`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.COCO17)        | COCO-17 (the 2D pose format), for reusing the canonicalization on 2.5D data. |

### Functions

| [`canonicalize_pose`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.canonicalize_pose)(landmarks, \*[, joints, scale])   | Express one frame's 3D landmarks `(K, C>=3)` in the pelvis frame `(K, 3)`.         |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`canonicalize_sequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.canonicalize_sequence)(world, \*[, joints, scale])   | Canonicalize every frame/person of a `(..., K, C)` landmark stack → `(..., K, 3)`. |
| [`pelvis_frame`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.pelvis_frame)(landmarks, \*[, joints])               | Anatomical frame of a single pose: `(pelvis_origin, R)`.                           |

### Classes

| [`BodyJoints`](_autosummary/kodokan.canon3d.html.md#kodokan.canon3d.BodyJoints)(l_hip, r_hip, l_shoulder, r_shoulder)   | Landmark indices needed to build the pelvis anatomical frame.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|

### kodokan.canon3d.BLAZEPOSE33 *= BodyJoints(l_hip=23, r_hip=24, l_shoulder=11, r_shoulder=12)*

MediaPipe BlazePose-33 (the repo’s 3D-lift output format).

### *class* kodokan.canon3d.BodyJoints(l_hip, r_hip, l_shoulder, r_shoulder)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Landmark indices needed to build the pelvis anatomical frame.

### kodokan.canon3d.COCO17 *= BodyJoints(l_hip=11, r_hip=12, l_shoulder=5, r_shoulder=6)*

COCO-17 (the 2D pose format), for reusing the canonicalization on 2.5D data.

### kodokan.canon3d.canonicalize_pose(landmarks, , joints=BodyJoints(l_hip=23, r_hip=24, l_shoulder=11, r_shoulder=12), scale=True)

Express one frame’s 3D landmarks `(K, C>=3)` in the pelvis frame `(K, 3)`.

Removes camera rotation + translation (and, with `scale=True`, subject size
by dividing by torso length). Columns beyond `xyz` (e.g. visibility) are
dropped; `nan` inputs propagate (so occluded frames stay droppable).

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### kodokan.canon3d.canonicalize_sequence(world, , joints=BodyJoints(l_hip=23, r_hip=24, l_shoulder=11, r_shoulder=12), scale=True)

Canonicalize every frame/person of a `(..., K, C)` landmark stack → `(..., K, 3)`.

Each frame (and person) is canonicalized to *its own* pelvis frame — the
viewpoint-invariant choice for pose-only technique features.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### kodokan.canon3d.pelvis_frame(landmarks, , joints=BodyJoints(l_hip=23, r_hip=24, l_shoulder=11, r_shoulder=12))

Anatomical frame of a single pose: `(pelvis_origin, R)`.

`R` (shape `(3, 3)`, rows are the new basis) maps world coordinates into
the subject frame: **x** = subject’s right (hip line), **y** = up
(pelvis→neck spine), **z** = forward (`y × x`). The hip line is
orthogonalized against the spine so the basis is orthonormal (Gram-Schmidt).

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, `ndarray`]


# _autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md

# kodokan.config

Where kodokan keeps its data (downloaded clips + derived artifacts).

Large/churny artifacts (videos, per-frame keypoints, rendered overlays) live
*outside* the repo by default — under `~/kodokan_data` — so they don’t bloat
the (Dropbox-synced) source tree. Override the root with the
`KODOKAN_DATA_DIR` environment variable.

On the dev Mac `~/kodokan_data` is a symlink into an off-machine-backed data
area; code addresses it transparently through the symlink either way. None of
this data is precious — every subfolder is downloaded or pipeline-derived; see
`misc/docs/regenerate-data.md` for how to rebuild it from scratch.

### Module Attributes

| [`KODOKAN_DATA_ENV`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.KODOKAN_DATA_ENV)            | Env var overriding the data root (default `~/kodokan_data`).                                                                                       |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SEGMENT_MIN_TWO_PERSON_FRAC`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.SEGMENT_MIN_TWO_PERSON_FRAC) | keep a detected demonstration only if both judoka are present for at least this fraction of its frames.                                            |
| [`EVAL_MIN_TWO_PERSON_FRAC`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.EVAL_MIN_TWO_PERSON_FRAC)    | Quality gate used when *consuming* stored demos for recognition/scoring/ catalog building: only trust demos where both judoka are clearly visible. |

### Functions

| [`clips_dir`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.clips_dir)()   | Directory holding downloaded video clips + their `*.info.json` sidecars.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`data_dir`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.data_dir)()    | Resolve the kodokan data root (`$KODOKAN_DATA_DIR` or `~/kodokan_data`).   |
| [`models_dir`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.models_dir)()  | Directory for downloaded model weights (kept out of the repo).             |
| [`pose_dir`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.pose_dir)()    | Directory holding extracted per-clip keypoint sequences (NPZ / Parquet).   |
| [`viz_dir`](_autosummary/kodokan.config.html.md#kodokan.config.viz_dir)()     | Directory holding rendered overlays (MP4) and Rerun recordings (RRD).      |

### kodokan.config.EVAL_MIN_TWO_PERSON_FRAC *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* *= 0.4*

Quality gate used when *consuming* stored demos for recognition/scoring/
catalog building: only trust demos where both judoka are clearly visible.
Stricter than the segmentation gate on purpose. Used by the eval harnesses,
[`kodokan.flashcards.build_catalog()`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.build_catalog), and scoring.

### kodokan.config.KODOKAN_DATA_ENV *= 'KODOKAN_DATA_DIR'*

Env var overriding the data root (default `~/kodokan_data`).

### kodokan.config.SEGMENT_MIN_TWO_PERSON_FRAC *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)* *= 0.3*

keep a detected demonstration
only if both judoka are present for at least this fraction of its frames.
Deliberately lenient — we would rather store a borderline demo (and filter it
later) than silently drop a real one. Used by the batch/segmentation step.

* **Type:**
  Inclusion gate used when *segmenting* a clip

# _autosummary/kodokan.descriptors.html.md

# kodokan.descriptors

Experimental per-demo feature descriptors (to test what makes throws separable).

The Stage-5 eval showed plain single-person joint angles don’t discriminate
technique (dominated by viewpoint + tori/uke role inconsistency). This module
offers alternative descriptors so the eval harness can measure which lever helps:

- `angles`      — primary person’s joint angles (the current baseline).
- `angles_vel`  — angles + their frame-to-frame velocity (dynamics).
- `angles_pos`  — angles + root-centered, torso-scaled keypoint positions.
- `angles_both` — both people’s joint angles, ordered by activity (captures the
  : tori/uke *interaction*, robust to which slot is which).
- `pos_both`    — both people’s normalized positions, activity-ordered.

All are 2D (still viewpoint-variant); the point is to isolate how much of the
failure is role/interaction/descriptor vs genuinely needing 3D.

### Functions

| [`demo_descriptor`](_autosummary/kodokan.descriptors.html.md#kodokan.descriptors.demo_descriptor)(pose_seq, start_s, end_s, \*)   | Per-frame feature matrix for one demo window under the chosen `mode`.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### kodokan.descriptors.demo_descriptor(pose_seq, start_s, end_s, , mode='angles')

Per-frame feature matrix for one demo window under the chosen `mode`.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`


# _autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md

# kodokan.flashcards

Technique-recognition learning game (app #6) — logic layer.

Help students learn to recognize/name throws. No throw-detection is needed (ground
truth is known): we generate multiple-choice problems from the clip library —
**name -> pick the video** or **video -> pick the name** — with *confusable*
distractors, log every response (timestamped, with the exact problem) for adaptive
learning, and score with confusion-aware weighting.

“Confusability” between techniques is a **pose-shape similarity** (closeness of their
mean pooled descriptors) — an honest proxy for visual confusability that does NOT
require a working recognizer (the cross-source recognizer is currently at chance). It
can be swapped for the model’s confusion matrix once recognition generalizes.

This module is the (UI-agnostic) logic + storage; a web UI plugs into it later.

### Functions

| [`build_catalog`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.build_catalog)(\*[, min_two_person_frac, ...])      | Build `{technique_key: {"name", "clips":[...]}}` from the pose/segments stores.                                 |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`build_confusability`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.build_confusability)([catalog, feature])            | Technique×technique similarity (0..1) from mean pooled pose descriptors.                                        |
| [`build_model_confusability`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.build_model_confusability)([catalog, ...])          | Technique×technique confusability from the recognizer's own leave-one-out confusions.                           |
| [`clip_filename`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.clip_filename)(video_id, start_s, dur_s)            | The web-app clip file for one demo segment, named by the segment's IDENTITY.                                    |
| [`confusable_distractors`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.confusable_distractors)(target_key, keys, \*, n)    | Pick `n` distractor keys, preferring those most confusable with the target.                                     |
| [`log_response`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.log_response)(problem, chosen_index, \*[, ...])     | Record a response (datetime + exact problem + choice + correctness + score).                                    |
| [`make_problem`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.make_problem)(catalog, target_key, \*[, mode, ...]) | Build a multiple-choice problem for `target_key` from a technique `catalog`.                                    |
| [`next_target`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.next_target)(keys, history, \*[, focus, rng])       | Pick the next technique to quiz: unseen and often-missed (within `focus`) first.                                |
| [`problem_from_keys`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.problem_from_keys)(catalog, target_key, ...)        | Assemble a [`Problem`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.Problem) from an already-chosen, ordered option set. |

One multiple-choice flashcard problem.

### kodokan.flashcards.build_catalog(, min_two_person_frac=None, min_demo_s=1.0, max_demos=None, segments=None)

Build `{technique_key: {"name", "clips":[...]}}` from the pose/segments stores.

Aggregates all sources: each clip contributes its demo intervals (for looping media),
so a technique present in several sources offers varied multiple-choice media.

`max_demos` caps the demos kept per source video (`None`, the default, keeps every
demo that passes the quality gate — #37: the store has 6–8 reps per video and all of
them are worth showing). `segments` is the `{video_id: record}` mapping to read
(default: [`kodokan.store.segments_store()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.segments_store)).

### kodokan.flashcards.build_confusability(catalog=None, , feature='tori_angles_pos')

Technique×technique similarity (0..1) from mean pooled pose descriptors.

`similarity[a][b]` high ⇒ techniques a, b look alike in pose-space (likely
confusable for a learner). An honest, recognizer-free proxy; swap for the model’s
confusion matrix once cross-source recognition works.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.flashcards.build_model_confusability(catalog=None, , feature='tori_angles_pos', method='lda_knn', cross_source=True)

Technique×technique confusability from the recognizer’s own leave-one-out confusions.

Same shape as [`build_confusability()`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.build_confusability). Predictions are leave-one-clip-out
(`cross_source`) or leave-one-sample-out. Techniques the model never confuses get
no row entries; `learning.merge_similarity` / the strategies fall back as usual.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.flashcards.clip_filename(video_id, start_s, dur_s)

The web-app clip file for one demo segment, named by the segment’s IDENTITY.

`{video_id}_{start_ms}_{dur_ms}.mp4`: the name says which time span of which source it
shows, so re-segmenting can never make an existing name show a different cut (#45) — a
changed segment simply gets a new name. Positional names (`{vid}_3.mp4`) could.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### kodokan.flashcards.confusable_distractors(target_key, keys, , n, similarity=None, rng=None)

Pick `n` distractor keys, preferring those most confusable with the target.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

### kodokan.flashcards.log_response(problem, chosen_index, , user='default', store=None, similarity=None, timestamp=None)

Record a response (datetime + exact problem + choice + correctness + score).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.flashcards.make_problem(catalog, target_key, , mode='video_to_name', n_choices=4, similarity=None, rng=None, clip_for=None)

Build a multiple-choice problem for `target_key` from a technique `catalog`.

`catalog` maps `technique_key -> {"name": str, "clips": [clip dicts]}`.
`clip_for(key)` returns a looping clip for a key (default: first clip); for
`name_to_video` the choices are clips, for `video_to_name` they are names.

* **Return type:**
  [`Problem`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.Problem)

### kodokan.flashcards.next_target(keys, history, , focus=None, rng=None)

Pick the next technique to quiz: unseen and often-missed (within `focus`) first.

Spaced-repetition-ish weight = (wrongs + 1) / (seen + 1): unseen -> 1, frequently
wrong -> high, mastered -> low. `history` is a list of response dicts.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### kodokan.flashcards.problem_from_keys(catalog, target_key, option_keys, , mode='video_to_name', clip_for=None, problem_id)

Assemble a [`Problem`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.Problem) from an already-chosen, ordered option set.

The seam between *choosing* (`make_problem`, or a `learning.Strategy`) and
*presenting*: whoever picks the options, the problem looks the same.

* **Return type:**
  [`Problem`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.Problem)

### kodokan.flashcards.responses_store(directory=None)

A dict-like JSON store of logged responses (per-user, timestamped).

### kodokan.flashcards.score_response(correct_key, chosen_key, , similarity=None, max_partial=0.5)

Confusion-weighted credit in [0, 1].

Correct = 1.0. A wrong answer earns *partial* credit proportional to how confusable
the chosen technique is with the correct one (an honest mistake between look-alike
throws is penalized less than confusing two obviously different throws).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/kodokan.html.md

# kodokan

kodokan — study Kodokan Judo throws from video via body-pose analysis.

A pipeline over the official *Kodokan 100 Techniques* YouTube playlist: acquire
clips + metadata, estimate per-frame two-person skeletons, segment each clip into
its repeated demonstrations, visualize skeletons (overlay-on-video and on a blank
canvas), and — later — recognize, compare, and score throws.

Quick start:

```default
from kodokan.acquire import download_techniques
from kodokan.pose import estimate_poses
from kodokan.viz import render_skeleton_video

res = download_techniques(playlist_items="2")          # Seoi-nage
seq = estimate_poses(res[0].path, source_url=res[0].info["webpage_url"])
render_skeleton_video(seq, out_path="overlay.mp4", source_video=res[0].path)
render_skeleton_video(seq, out_path="skeleton.mp4", blank_canvas=True)
```

See `misc/docs/research-architecture.md` for the tool/architecture rationale.

### *class* kodokan.LiveTechniqueTest(test, \*, fps, featurize=<function pooled_demo_descriptor>, angle_featurize=<function demo_features>, on_prompt=None, \*\*detector_kwargs)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The test loop on a live stream: prompt, detect the throw, grade, prompt again.

[`push()`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.LiveTechniqueTest.push) takes one frame and returns `(segment, result)` for each throw that
closed with it; after each graded throw the next technique is drawn
(`prompt`). Detector options pass through.

A throw is graded once it has *closed* (`close_after_s` after it ends), so the
performer should wait for the next prompt before the next throw; any motion the
detector takes for a throw also uses up a prompt.

#### push(keypoints, frame_index=None)

Add one frame; grade each throw it closed and draw the next prompt.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment), [`TestResult`](_autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md#kodokan.testmode.TestResult)]]

### *class* kodokan.TechniqueTest(recognizer, , pool=None, references=None, lang='en', confidence_weight=0.5, seed=None, rng=None, advice={'en': {'close': 'Close to the reference: keep it up.', 'elbow': "Your {side} elbow is {deg:.0f}° off the reference: keep that arm's pull firm and close to your body.", 'headline': '{technique}: {score}/100.', 'hip': 'Your {side} hip is {deg:.0f}° off: bring your hips lower and closer to your partner.', 'kake': 'Most of the difference is in kake: commit through the finish.', 'knee': 'Your {side} knee is {deg:.0f}° off: bend your knees more as you enter, then drive up.', 'kuzushi': "Most of the difference is in kuzushi: break your partner's balance before you turn in.", 'shoulder': "Your {side} shoulder is {deg:.0f}° off: lift and turn that arm with the reference timing to take your partner's balance.", 'tsukuri': 'Most of the difference is in tsukuri: step in faster and closer.'}, 'fr': {'close': 'Proche de la référence : continuez ainsi.', 'elbow': "Votre coude {side} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° de la référence : gardez la traction de ce bras ferme et près du corps.", 'headline': '{technique} : {score}/100.', 'hip': "Votre hanche {side_f} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° : placez vos hanches plus bas et plus près de votre partenaire.", 'kake': "L'essentiel de l'écart est dans le kake : allez au bout de la projection.", 'knee': "Votre genou {side} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° : fléchissez davantage les genoux en entrant, puis poussez vers le haut.", 'kuzushi': "L'essentiel de l'écart est dans le kuzushi : déséquilibrez votre partenaire avant d'entrer.", 'shoulder': "Votre épaule {side_f} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° : levez et tournez ce bras au rythme de la référence pour déséquilibrer votre partenaire.", 'tsukuri': "L'essentiel de l'écart est dans le tsukuri : entrez plus vite et plus près."}})

* **Parameters:**

    also graded on closeness, with advice.

    rest from closeness to the reference, when there is one).

### *class* kodokan.ThrowDetector(\*, fps, width=0, height=0, buffer_s=20.0, close_after_s=1.0, segmenter=<function motion_segments>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A rolling pose buffer that reports each throw once, after its segment closes.

Push one frame at a time (`(P, 17, 3)` keypoints, as in [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.PoseSequence)).
[`push()`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.ThrowDetector.push) returns `(buffer, segment)` for the throws that closed with that
frame. A segment counts as closed when it ends at least `close_after_s` before
the newest frame; the buffer keeps the last `buffer_s` seconds of pushed frames
(at `fps` frames a second: push every analysed frame, or pass the analysed rate
as `fps`). A segment that mostly overlaps a throw already reported is that throw.

#### buffer()

The buffered frames as a [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.PoseSequence) (people padded with NaN).

* **Return type:**
  [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence)

#### push(keypoints, frame_index=None)

Add one frame; return `(buffer, segment)` for each throw it closed.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence), [`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment)]]

### kodokan.build_catalog(, min_two_person_frac=None, min_demo_s=1.0, max_demos=None, segments=None)

Build `{technique_key: {"name", "clips":[...]}}` from the pose/segments stores.

Aggregates all sources: each clip contributes its demo intervals (for looping media),
so a technique present in several sources offers varied multiple-choice media.

`max_demos` caps the demos kept per source video (`None`, the default, keeps every
demo that passes the quality gate — #37: the store has 6–8 reps per video and all of
them are worth showing). `segments` is the `{video_id: record}` mapping to read
(default: [`kodokan.store.segments_store()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.segments_store)).

### kodokan.build_confusability(catalog=None, , feature='tori_angles_pos')

Technique×technique similarity (0..1) from mean pooled pose descriptors.

`similarity[a][b]` high ⇒ techniques a, b look alike in pose-space (likely
confusable for a learner). An honest, recognizer-free proxy; swap for the model’s
confusion matrix once cross-source recognition works.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.build_reference(feature_list)

Pick the medoid demo as reference and record the baseline distance spread.

Returns `{medoid, reference, baseline, distance_matrix}` where `baseline` is
the array of normalized-DTW distances from every other demo to the medoid.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.clip_filename(video_id, start_s, dur_s)

The web-app clip file for one demo segment, named by the segment’s IDENTITY.

`{video_id}_{start_ms}_{dur_ms}.mp4`: the name says which time span of which source it
shows, so re-segmenting can never make an existing name show a different cut (#45) — a
changed segment simply gets a new name. Positional names (`{vid}_3.mp4`) could.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### kodokan.coach(query_features, reference, , technique=None, lang='en', n_tips=2, min_deviation_deg=10.0, advice={'en': {'close': 'Close to the reference: keep it up.', 'elbow': "Your {side} elbow is {deg:.0f}° off the reference: keep that arm's pull firm and close to your body.", 'headline': '{technique}: {score}/100.', 'hip': 'Your {side} hip is {deg:.0f}° off: bring your hips lower and closer to your partner.', 'kake': 'Most of the difference is in kake: commit through the finish.', 'knee': 'Your {side} knee is {deg:.0f}° off: bend your knees more as you enter, then drive up.', 'kuzushi': "Most of the difference is in kuzushi: break your partner's balance before you turn in.", 'shoulder': "Your {side} shoulder is {deg:.0f}° off: lift and turn that arm with the reference timing to take your partner's balance.", 'tsukuri': 'Most of the difference is in tsukuri: step in faster and closer.'}, 'fr': {'close': 'Proche de la référence : continuez ainsi.', 'elbow': "Votre coude {side} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° de la référence : gardez la traction de ce bras ferme et près du corps.", 'headline': '{technique} : {score}/100.', 'hip': "Votre hanche {side_f} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° : placez vos hanches plus bas et plus près de votre partenaire.", 'kake': "L'essentiel de l'écart est dans le kake : allez au bout de la projection.", 'knee': "Votre genou {side} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° : fléchissez davantage les genoux en entrant, puis poussez vers le haut.", 'kuzushi': "L'essentiel de l'écart est dans le kuzushi : déséquilibrez votre partenaire avant d'entrer.", 'shoulder': "Votre épaule {side_f} s'écarte de {deg:.0f}° : levez et tournez ce bras au rythme de la référence pour déséquilibrer votre partenaire.", 'tsukuri': "L'essentiel de l'écart est dans le tsukuri : entrez plus vite et plus près."}})

Score `query_features` against `reference` and advise on the worst dimensions.

* **Parameters:**
  * **query_features** (`ndarray`) – per-frame joint angles of the performance
    (`kodokan.score.demo_features()`).
  * **reference** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – the target technique’s `build_reference()`.
  * **lang** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a key of `advice` (`"en"` or `"fr"` built in).
  * **n_tips** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – joint tips to give, worst first, after the phase tip.
  * **min_deviation_deg** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – a phase or joint closer than this gets no tip; with
    none left, the advice says the performance is close to the reference.
* **Return type:**
  [`Coaching`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.Coaching)

A window with fewer than two usable frames cannot be compared: it gets a
[`Coaching`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.Coaching) with no score and `reason="too_short"` rather than an error,
so a live loop goes on.

### kodokan.estimate_poses(video_path, , backend='rtmlib', n_persons=2, conf_thresh=0.3, frame_step=1, frame_range=None, device=None, source_url=None, progress=True, \*\*backend_kwargs)

Estimate per-frame, per-person COCO-17 keypoints for a video clip.

Simplest use: `estimate_poses("clip.mp4")` → a [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.PoseSequence) with the
two highest-confidence people per frame (left→right ordered) via RTMPose.

* **Parameters:**
  * **video_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Path to the video clip.
  * **backend** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"rtmlib"` (RTMPose top-down, CPU/ONNX; default, and the
    only one installed by `kodokan[pose]`) or `"ultralytics"`
    (YOLO11-pose, MPS), which needs `kodokan[track]` — an
    AGPL-3.0-or-later dependency, see the README’s
    “Licensing of extras”.
  * **n_persons** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of person slots to keep per frame (2 for tori+uke).
  * **conf_thresh** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Minimum mean per-person confidence to keep a detection.
  * **frame_step** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Analyze every `frame_step`-th frame (1 = every frame).
  * **frame_range** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional `(start, stop)` frame index window.
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Backend device (`"cpu"`/`"mps"`); backend default if `None`.
  * **source_url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Canonical source URL to record as provenance.
  * **progress** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Print a progress line periodically.
  * **\*\*backend_kwargs** – Forwarded to the backend (e.g. `mode="performance"`
    for rtmlib, or `model_name="yolo11m-pose.pt"` for ultralytics).
* **Return type:**
  [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence)
* **Returns:**
  A [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.html.md#kodokan.PoseSequence) of shape `(F, n_persons, 17, 3)`.

### kodokan.estimate_poses_tracked(video_path, , n_persons=2, tracker='botsort.yaml', conf_thresh=0.3, max_gap_frac=0.15, stale_after=12, frame_step=1, frame_range=None, device='mps', model_name='yolo11n-pose.pt', source_url=None, progress=True)

Estimate per-frame keypoints with persistent tori/uke identity.

Returns a [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence) whose person slots are *stable*
across the clip (slot 0 = the track that is, on average, further left).

* **Parameters:**
  * **video_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Path to the clip.
  * **n_persons** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of stable identity slots to keep (2 for tori+uke).
  * **tracker** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Ultralytics tracker config (`"botsort.yaml"` or `"bytetrack.yaml"`).
  * **conf_thresh** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Minimum mean per-person confidence to count a detection.
  * **frame_step** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Analyze every n-th frame.
  * **frame_range** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional `(start, stop)` frame window.
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Torch device (`"mps"`/`"cpu"`).
  * **model_name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – YOLO-pose weights (resolved under the data models dir).
  * **source_url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Provenance URL.
  * **progress** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Print progress.
* **Return type:**
  [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence)

`catalog` maps `technique_key -> {"name": str, "clips": [clip dicts]}`.

### kodokan.next_target(keys, history, , focus=None, rng=None)

Pick the next technique to quiz: unseen and often-missed (within `focus`) first.

Spaced-repetition-ish weight = (wrongs + 1) / (seen + 1): unseen -> 1, frequently
wrong -> high, mastered -> low. `history` is a list of response dicts.

### kodokan.score(query_features, reference)

Score a query against a reference, calibrated to the genuine-demo spread.

`score` is 0–100: 100 ≈ as close as the closest genuine demo, 0 ≈ as far as the
90th-percentile (or worse). `closer_than_pct` is the percent of genuine demos
the query is closer-to-reference than.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.score_response(correct_key, chosen_key, , similarity=None, max_partial=0.5)

Confusion-weighted credit in [0, 1].

Correct = 1.0. A wrong answer earns *partial* credit proportional to how confusable
the chosen technique is with the correct one (an honest mistake between look-alike
throws is penalized less than confusing two obviously different throws).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### kodokan.segment_demonstrations(pose_seq, , video_path=None, use_optical_flow=False, min_two_person_frac=0.0, \*\*find_kwargs)

Find demonstrations, annotate each with its two-person coverage, and gate.

Uses pose motion energy by default (fuse optical flow with `use_optical_flow`).
Segments whose two-person coverage is below `min_two_person_frac` are dropped
(a throw demonstration needs both tori and uke), then re-indexed in time order.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment)]

A dict-like `{video_id: <json>}` store for demo segments (and metadata).

# _autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md

# kodokan.learning

Adaptive learning engine for the flashcard quiz — selectable strategies.

A [`Strategy`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.Strategy) maps the recorded response **history** to the next **problem**
— which technique to ask (target) and which distractors to show — both drawn from
an active study *set*. Strategies are research-backed (spaced repetition + MCQ
learning science; see `misc/docs/learning-research.md`) and the user picks one in
settings. The function from recorded data → next question is therefore a swappable
strategy (open/closed): add a class, register it, and it appears in the UI.

## Design notes

- History is a list of plain response dicts (the logged record schema below), so the
  engine has no storage dependency and is trivially testable.
- Per-item adaptive state (Leitner box, SM-2 ease, FSRS stability) is reconstructed by
  *replaying* the history — no mutable server state to corrupt.
- Spacing intervals are in **days**; within a single dense session most items aren’t
  “due”, so every scheduler falls back to an urgency ranking (most-overdue / lowest
  recall / box weight) instead of stalling.

Record schema (one dict per answered problem):

```default
response_id, problem_id, user, session_id, strategy_key,
target_key, mode, choice_keys, chosen_key,
correct, score, timed_out, response_time_ms,
ts_presented, ts_answered            # ISO-8601 UTC
```

### Functions

| [`empirical_confusion`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.empirical_confusion)(history, \*[, ...])           | Per-learner confusion matrix from wrong answers: `{correct: {chosen_wrong: weight}}`.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`item_accuracy`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.item_accuracy)(history)                            | Per-item running stats: `{key: {n, wrong, last_ts, last_correct}}`.                     |
| [`list_strategies`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.list_strategies)()                                 | Describe available strategies (for the settings UI).                                    |
| [`make_strategy`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.make_strategy)([key])                              | Instantiate a strategy by key (default = confusion-weighted); unknown params ignored.   |
| [`merge_similarity`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.merge_similarity)(base, overlay, \*[, boost])      | Additively merge two `target -> {key: weight}` matrices (overlay boosted).              |
| [`pick_distractors`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.pick_distractors)(target, study_set, \*, n[, ...]) | Pick `n` distractors from `study_set`, preferring confusable ones.                      |

### kodokan.learning.empirical_confusion(history, , halflife_days=7.0, now=None)

Per-learner confusion matrix from wrong answers: `{correct: {chosen_wrong: weight}}`.

Each mistake contributes a recency-decayed, partial-credit-shortfall weight, so the
throws a learner *actually* mixes up (recently) dominate.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### kodokan.learning.make_strategy(key=None, \*\*params)

Instantiate a strategy by key (default = confusion-weighted); unknown params ignored.

* **Return type:**
  [`Strategy`](_autosummary/kodokan.learning.html.md#kodokan.learning.Strategy)

### kodokan.learning.merge_similarity(base, overlay, , boost=2.0)

Additively merge two `target -> {key: weight}` matrices (overlay boosted).

Keeps the dense `base` (pose-shape) for every target and *adds* the sparse
`overlay` (per-learner confusion) on top — so confusable distractors are always
available, with the learner’s personal confusers weighted up rather than replacing
pose-similarity for not-yet-confused targets.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.learning.pick_distractors(target, study_set, , n, similarity=None, rng, top_up=True)

Pick `n` distractors from `study_set`, preferring confusable ones.

`similarity` maps `target -> {key: weight}` (pose-shape or empirical confusion).
Falls back to uniform when absent; tops up from the rest of the set if the
confusable pool is too small (so the answer set always has `n` options when possible).


# _autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md

# kodokan.pose

Body-pose estimation: a video → a sequence of per-person skeletal keypoints.

A single [`estimate_poses()`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.estimate_poses) facade with a pluggable, multi-person backend
(`rtmlib` = RTMPose top-down, default; or `ultralytics` = YOLO11-pose). Both
emit the **COCO-17** keypoint layout, so downstream code is backend-agnostic.

Judo throws involve two people in close contact, so the default keeps the
`n_persons` highest-confidence detections per frame and orders them left→right
(a crude tori/uke proxy that is good enough for visualization and for the first
“compare two demos” experiments; true identity tracking through the occluded
apex of a throw is a separate, harder problem — see `misc/docs/research-architecture.md`).

Output is a [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence): an `(F, P, 17, 3)` array (x, y, confidence;
`NaN` where a person slot is empty in that frame), plus the frame indices, fps,
and source provenance.

### Module Attributes

| [`COCO17_KEYPOINTS`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.COCO17_KEYPOINTS)   | COCO-17 keypoint names, in index order.                                     |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`COCO17_SKELETON`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.COCO17_SKELETON)    | COCO-17 skeleton edges (pairs of keypoint indices) for drawing/connections. |

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### kodokan.pose.estimate_poses(video_path, , backend='rtmlib', n_persons=2, conf_thresh=0.3, frame_step=1, frame_range=None, device=None, source_url=None, progress=True, \*\*backend_kwargs)

Estimate per-frame, per-person COCO-17 keypoints for a video clip.

Simplest use: `estimate_poses("clip.mp4")` → a [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence) with the
two highest-confidence people per frame (left→right ordered) via RTMPose.

* **Parameters:**
  * **video_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Path to the video clip.
  * **backend** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"rtmlib"` (RTMPose top-down, CPU/ONNX; default, and the
    only one installed by `kodokan[pose]`) or `"ultralytics"`
    (YOLO11-pose, MPS), which needs `kodokan[track]` — an
    AGPL-3.0-or-later dependency, see the README’s
    “Licensing of extras”.
  * **n_persons** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of person slots to keep per frame (2 for tori+uke).
  * **conf_thresh** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Minimum mean per-person confidence to keep a detection.
  * **frame_step** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Analyze every `frame_step`-th frame (1 = every frame).
  * **frame_range** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional `(start, stop)` frame index window.
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Backend device (`"cpu"`/`"mps"`); backend default if `None`.
  * **source_url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Canonical source URL to record as provenance.
  * **progress** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Print a progress line periodically.
  * **\*\*backend_kwargs** – Forwarded to the backend (e.g. `mode="performance"`
    for rtmlib, or `model_name="yolo11m-pose.pt"` for ultralytics).
* **Return type:**
  [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence)
* **Returns:**
  A [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence) of shape `(F, n_persons, 17, 3)`.


# _autosummary/kodokan.quiz.html.md

# kodokan.quiz

Quiz service: the UI-agnostic orchestrator of the technique-recognition game (app #6).

`flashcards` makes and scores one problem, `learning` chooses the next one from a
learner’s history. This module wires them to storage so that any surface (a web app, a
CLI, a test) needs only three calls, all taking and returning plain data:

```default
quiz = Quiz(catalog, similarity=similarity)          # or Quiz.from_library()
problem = quiz.next_problem("ana", strategy="sm2")   # issued problems are remembered
record = quiz.submit(problem.problem_id, chosen_index=2, response_time_ms=3100)
quiz.stats("ana")                                    # per-technique {n, wrong, ...}
```

State lives in two dict-like stores (seams; default: `dol` JSON files under the data
root, one per user prefix): the **issued problems** not yet answered, and the **responses**
(one record per answered problem, the `learning.RECORD_FIELDS` schema). A surface can
therefore be stateless between “give me a problem” and “here is the answer”.

```pycon
>>> catalog = {k: {"name": k.title(), "clips": []} for k in ("seoinage", "ogoshi", "tomoenage", "uchimata")}
>>> quiz = Quiz(catalog, responses={}, problems={})
>>> problem = quiz.next_problem("ana", rng=__import__("random").Random(0))
>>> record = quiz.submit(problem.problem_id, problem.correct_index)
>>> record["correct"], record["user"], quiz.stats("ana")[problem.target_key]["n"]
(True, 'ana', 1)
```

### Module Attributes

| [`USER_RE`](_autosummary/kodokan.quiz.html.md#kodokan.quiz.USER_RE)   | A user id is a filesystem-safe token; `__` is the separator of the stored keys.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`quiz_stores`](_autosummary/kodokan.quiz.html.md#kodokan.quiz.quiz_stores)([directory])   | `(responses, problems)` as `dol` JSON-file stores under the data root.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Quiz`](_autosummary/kodokan.quiz.html.md#kodokan.quiz.Quiz)(catalog[, similarity, responses, ...])   | The game for one `catalog` (`technique_key -> {"name", "clips"}`).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* kodokan.quiz.Quiz(catalog, similarity=None, responses=None, problems=None, clip_for=None, now=<function \_now>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The game for one `catalog` (`technique_key -> {"name", "clips"}`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **similarity** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `target -> {key: weight}`, e.g. `flashcards.build_confusability()`;
    the learner’s own confusion is merged on top by the strategy.
  * **responses** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)) – answered-problem records, keyed `<user>__<ts>__<response_id>.json`.
  * **problems** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)) – issued, unanswered problems, keyed `<problem_id>.json`.
    Both default to [`quiz_stores()`](_autosummary/kodokan.quiz.html.md#kodokan.quiz.quiz_stores).
  * **clip_for** ([`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)) – `key -> clip` for the media of a technique (default: its first clip).

#### *classmethod* from_library(\*\*kwargs)

A quiz over the clip library on disk (needs `kodokan[analysis]`).

`confusability`: `"pose"` (default, pose-shape proxy) or `"model"` (the
recognizer’s leave-one-clip-out confusions; weak until cross-source recognition
beats chance, #7). An explicit `similarity=` mapping wins over both.

* **Return type:**
  [`Quiz`](_autosummary/kodokan.quiz.html.md#kodokan.quiz.Quiz)

#### history(user)

The user’s answered-problem records, oldest first.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### next_problem(user, , strategy=None, mode='video_to_name', study_set=None, session_id=None, rng=None)

Choose the next problem for `user` from their history, and remember it as issued.

* **Parameters:**
  * **strategy** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – a key of [`strategies()`](_autosummary/kodokan.quiz.html.md#kodokan.quiz.Quiz.strategies) (default: confusion-weighted).
  * **study_set** – the technique keys to draw from (default: the whole catalog).
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – for an unknown user format, mode, or an empty study set.
* **Return type:**
  [`Problem`](_autosummary/kodokan.flashcards.html.md#kodokan.flashcards.Problem)

#### stats(user)

Per-technique `{n, wrong, last_ts, last_correct}` for the user.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### *static* strategies()

The selectable strategies (for a settings screen).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### submit(problem_id, chosen_index, , timed_out=False, response_time_ms=None)

Score an issued problem, store the record, and return it.

`chosen_index` is None for a timeout. A problem is answered once.

* **Raises:**
  * [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – if `problem_id` was never issued, or was already answered.
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – if `chosen_index` is not one of the choices.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# _autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md

# kodokan.recognize

Learned-vs-DTW technique recognition experiments (data-appropriate, no GPU).

The feature bake-off showed DTW on hand-crafted angles can’t tell techniques apart.
This module tests whether the bottleneck is the *classifier*, the *features*, or
tori/uke *role inconsistency*, with leave-one-out CV on the small dataset:

- feature modes: `primary_angles` (baseline), `tori_angles` (role-consistent —
  tori picked as the person left standing), `tori_angles_pos`.
- methods: `dtw_1nn` (DTW nearest-neighbour), `pool_centroid` / `pool_knn`
  (temporal-pyramid pooled descriptor + nearest-centroid / kNN), and `pool_lda_knn`
  (LDA-reduced + kNN, if scikit-learn is available).

Everything is numpy (sklearn optional), appropriate for ~80 samples where deep nets
would overfit; the same harness scales to more techniques once more data is collected.

### Functions

| [`classification_metrics`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.classification_metrics)(y_true, y_pred, \*[, ...])   | Top-1, balanced (macro-recall), majority-class baseline, n_classes, n.                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`confusion_pairs`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.confusion_pairs)(y_true, y_pred, \*[, top])          | Most-frequent misclassifications as `{true, pred, count}` (off-diagonal).                                                     |
| [`demo_feature`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.demo_feature)(pose_seq, start_s, end_s, \*, mode)    | Per-frame features for one demo under a role/feature mode.                                                                    |
| `dtw_1nn_accuracy`(feature_seqs, labels)                                                             |                                                                                                                               |
| [`dtw_1nn_predict`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.dtw_1nn_predict)(feature_seqs, labels)               | Leave-one-out 1-NN by DTW distance; returns predicted label per item.                                                         |
| [`loo_medoid_separability`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.loo_medoid_separability)(feats_by_tech, \*, ...)     | Leak-free (leave-one-demo-out medoid) technique-separability report.                                                          |
| [`loo_pooled_predict`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.loo_pooled_predict)(X, y, \*[, method, k, ...])      | Leave-one-out (or leave-one-GROUP-out) predictions; preprocessing fit on train only.                                          |
| [`mirror_feature`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.mirror_feature)(feat, \*, mode)                      | Per-frame features of the horizontally mirrored demo, from [`demo_feature()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.demo_feature)'s. |
| [`paired_bootstrap_separability`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.paired_bootstrap_separability)(rows_a, rows_b, \*)   | 95% percentile-bootstrap CIs for A, B and the PAIRED difference A−B.                                                          |
| `pool_centroid_accuracy`(X, y)                                                                       |                                                                                                                               |
| `pool_knn_accuracy`(X, y[, k])                                                                       |                                                                                                                               |
| `pool_lda_knn_accuracy`(X, y[, k])                                                                   |                                                                                                                               |
| [`pooled_descriptor`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.pooled_descriptor)(feat, \*[, levels])               | Temporal-pyramid pooled fixed-length descriptor (mean+std per segment).                                                       |
| [`roc_auc_distances`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.roc_auc_distances)(genuine, impostor)                | Standard ROC-AUC for a *distance* score: `P(impostor > genuine)` (ties=0.5).                                                  |
| [`similarity_from_confusion`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.similarity_from_confusion)(y_true, y_pred, \*)       | `target -> {other: weight}` (0..1) from a recognizer's confusions.                                                            |
| [`tori_decision`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.tori_decision)(pose_seq, start_s, end_s, \*[, ...])  | Tori (thrower) heuristic with a confidence margin and an abstain flag.                                                        |
| [`tori_decision_stats`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.tori_decision_stats)(decisions)                      | Aggregate fall-back / abstain rates and median margin over decisions.                                                         |
