### Classes

| [`ToriDecision`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.ToriDecision)(index, margin, fell_back, abstained)   | Outcome of the tori/uke role heuristic, with a confidence margin.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* kodokan.recognize.ToriDecision(index, margin, fell_back, abstained)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Outcome of the tori/uke role heuristic, with a confidence margin.

The “role-consistency is the dominant recognition lever” claim rests on this
heuristic, so — per the adversarial review — every call is now instrumented.

#### index

Chosen tori slot (always a usable slot, even when abstaining).

* **Type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### margin

Finish-frame hip-y separation between the two judoka in
*torso-length* units (how much lower uke’s hips sit than tori’s).
Larger = more confident; `nan` when the cue was unusable.

* **Type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### fell_back

The hip-y cue was unusable, so the most-present slot was used.

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### abstained

Low-confidence decision (`margin` below the abstain
threshold, or a fall-back) — the role label should not be trusted.

* **Type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### kodokan.recognize.classification_metrics(y_true, y_pred, , n_boot=0, seed=0)

Top-1, balanced (macro-recall), majority-class baseline, n_classes, n.

Pass `n_boot > 0` to add 95% percentile-bootstrap confidence intervals
(`top1_ci`/`balanced_ci`) — the rigor the review asked for, so small-n
accuracy differences aren’t over-read. Default `n_boot=0` is unchanged.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.recognize.confusion_pairs(y_true, y_pred, , top=None)

Most-frequent misclassifications as `{true, pred, count}` (off-diagonal).

Per-class confusion that stays readable at many classes: instead of a dense
N×N matrix it returns only the non-zero true→pred error cells, sorted by
count. A `pred` of `-1` means an abstain/no-prediction.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### kodokan.recognize.demo_feature(pose_seq, start_s, end_s, , mode)

Per-frame features for one demo under a role/feature mode.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### kodokan.recognize.dtw_1nn_predict(feature_seqs, labels)

Leave-one-out 1-NN by DTW distance; returns predicted label per item.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

### kodokan.recognize.loo_medoid_separability(feats_by_tech, , distance, per_demo=False)

Leak-free (leave-one-demo-out medoid) technique-separability report.

The earlier feature bake-off built each technique’s medoid reference from
*all* its demos, including the one being tested — so genuine distances were
optimistically low and needed an ad-hoc self-zero filter. Here a held-out
demo’s GENUINE distance is measured to the medoid of its technique’s *other*
demos (true leave-one-out, no self-zero), and its IMPOSTOR distances to every
other technique’s medoid. Reports leave-one-out nearest-medoid accuracy and
the standard ROC-AUC ([`roc_auc_distances()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.roc_auc_distances)).

* **Parameters:**
  * **feats_by_tech** ([`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)) – per technique, a list of per-demo feature arrays.
  * **distance** – `(feat_a, feat_b) -> float` (e.g. normalized DTW).
  * **per_demo** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – also return `per_demo` — one `{tech, genuine, impostor, correct}`
    per held-out demo, in input order — so callers can bootstrap without
    recomputing distances (see [`paired_bootstrap_separability()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.paired_bootstrap_separability)).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.recognize.loo_pooled_predict(X, y, , method='lda_knn', k=3, groups=None, X_aug=None)

Leave-one-out (or leave-one-GROUP-out) predictions; preprocessing fit on train only.

If `groups` is given (e.g. source `video_id` per sample), each fold excludes ALL
samples sharing the held-out sample’s group — i.e. **leave-one-clip-out**, which removes
within-clip leakage. Otherwise it is plain leave-one-sample-out.

`X_aug` (same shape as `X`, row `j` an augmented copy of sample `j`, e.g. the
pooled [`mirror_feature()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.mirror_feature)) adds the copies of the TRAIN-fold samples to each
fold’s training set; a held-out sample’s own copy (and its group’s) never trains.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### kodokan.recognize.mirror_feature(feat, , mode)

Per-frame features of the horizontally mirrored demo, from [`demo_feature()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.demo_feature)’s.

`mirror_feature(demo_feature(seq, ...), mode=m)` equals `demo_feature` of the
mirrored `seq` (tested), so mirrored training copies cost no pose estimation.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### kodokan.recognize.paired_bootstrap_separability(rows_a, rows_b, , n_boot=2000, seed=0)

95% percentile-bootstrap CIs for A, B and the PAIRED difference A−B.

`rows_a`/`rows_b` are `per_demo` outputs of [`loo_medoid_separability()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.loo_medoid_separability)
over the SAME demos in the same order (e.g. two modalities on identical frames), so
each resample draws the same demos for both — the difference CI then reflects only
the modality, not which demos happened to be drawn. Distances are reused, not
recomputed. A difference CI that straddles 0 means “not distinguishable at this n”.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.recognize.pooled_descriptor(feat, , levels=(1, 2, 4))

Temporal-pyramid pooled fixed-length descriptor (mean+std per segment).

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### kodokan.recognize.roc_auc_distances(genuine, impostor)

Standard ROC-AUC for a *distance* score: `P(impostor > genuine)` (ties=0.5).

Equals the Mann–Whitney U statistic divided by `|genuine|·|impostor|` — the
“standard ROC-AUC” the review asked for (replacing the ad-hoc self-zero-dropping
estimate). Larger = better separation (impostor demos sit farther than genuine
ones). NaNs are dropped; returns `nan` if either side is empty.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### kodokan.recognize.similarity_from_confusion(y_true, y_pred, , symmetric=True)

`target -> {other: weight}` (0..1) from a recognizer’s confusions.

`weight` is the share of `target`’s samples predicted as `other` (off-diagonal
only; abstains and self-predictions are ignored). With `symmetric` (default) the
weight is the mean of both directions, so “a looks like b” implies “b looks like a”,
which suits distractor choice. Same shape as `flashcards.build_confusability`, so it
plugs into `Quiz(similarity=...)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.recognize.tori_decision(pose_seq, start_s, end_s, , abstain_margin=0.15)

Tori (thrower) heuristic with a confidence margin and an abstain flag.

Tori is the judoka whose hips stay highest (smallest image-y) over the last
third of the demo — uke has been thrown to the ground. The margin is the two
judoka’s finish hip-y separation in torso-length units; below
`abstain_margin` (or when the cue is unusable and we fall back to presence)
the role assignment is unreliable and `abstained` is set. See
[`tori_decision_stats()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.tori_decision_stats) for aggregate fall-back/abstain rates.

* **Return type:**
  [`ToriDecision`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.ToriDecision)

### kodokan.recognize.tori_decision_stats(decisions)

Aggregate fall-back / abstain rates and median margin over decisions.

The instrumentation the review asked for: run this over every demo’s
[`tori_decision()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.tori_decision) to see how often the “dominant lever” heuristic is
actually confident vs. abstaining.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.recognize.tori_index(pose_seq, start_s, end_s)

Heuristic tori slot (thin wrapper over [`tori_decision()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.tori_decision)).

Backward-compatible: returns just the chosen slot. Use [`tori_decision()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#kodokan.recognize.tori_decision)
when you need the confidence margin / abstain flag.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)


# _autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md

# kodokan.recognizer

Technique recognition for applications: top-k guesses with inspectable scores (#3).

[`kodokan.recognize`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognize.html.md#module-kodokan.recognize) holds the research tools (features, LOO evaluation, metrics).
This module is the application facade over them:

- [`TechniqueRecognizer`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.TechniqueRecognizer) — fit on pooled demo descriptors, then
  [`recognize()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.TechniqueRecognizer.recognize) returns a [`Recognition`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.Recognition): the top-k
  [`Guess`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.Guess) es *and* the score of every technique (the intermediate vector a UI
  > can show).
- [`recognize_segments()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.recognize_segments) — offline video: detect the throws in a whole pose
  sequence and recognize each.
- [`ThrowDetector`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.ThrowDetector) — a rolling pose buffer that reports each throw once its
  segment has closed; [`LiveRecognizer`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.LiveRecognizer) recognizes them (live stream mode).

Scores are a softmax over negative distances to each technique’s centroid, in the
train-standardized (and, when scikit-learn is installed, LDA-projected) descriptor
space, with distances in units of the typical within-technique spread (measured
leave-one-out, as a held-out demo would see it). They rank techniques and sum to 1;
they are not calibrated probabilities. The LDA projection is still fit on every
training demo, so with few demos per technique the spread stays optimistic.

```pycon
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> X = np.vstack([rng.normal(c, 0.3, size=(5, 4)) for c in (0.0, 3.0, 6.0)])
>>> y = np.repeat(["seoi-nage", "o-goshi", "uchi-mata"], 5)
>>> rec = TechniqueRecognizer(method="centroid").fit(X, y)
>>> r = rec.recognize(np.full(4, 3.1), k=2)
>>> r.guesses[0].technique, len(r.guesses), round(sum(r.scores.values()), 6)
('o-goshi', 2, 1.0)
```

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A rolling pose buffer that reports each throw once, after its segment closes.

Push one frame at a time (`(P, 17, 3)` keypoints, as in `PoseSequence`).
[`push()`](_autosummary/kodokan.recognizer.html.md#kodokan.recognizer.ThrowDetector.push) returns `(buffer, segment)` for the throws that closed with that
frame. A segment counts as closed when it ends at least `close_after_s` before
the newest frame; the buffer keeps the last `buffer_s` seconds of pushed frames
(at `fps` frames a second: push every analysed frame, or pass the analysed rate
as `fps`). A segment that mostly overlaps a throw already reported is that throw.

#### buffer()

The buffered frames as a `PoseSequence` (people padded with NaN).

* **Return type:**
  [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence)

#### push(keypoints, frame_index=None)

Add one frame; return `(buffer, segment)` for each throw it closed.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence), [`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment)]]

# _autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md

# kodokan.segment

Segment a clip into its repeated demonstrations of one throw.

A Kodokan demo clip shows the *same* throw several times (varying speed/angle/
position), each demonstration a burst of whole-body motion bracketed by a
low-motion “reset” (walk back, re-grip, bow). Scene-cut detection finds nothing
in a continuous take, so we segment by **rhythm**: build a 1-D motion-energy
signal and take the high-motion runs as demonstrations (research §5).

Robustness pieces:

- **Hysteresis thresholding** — a demo turns *on* above `high_quantile` and stays
  on until energy drops below `low_quantile`. This stops *slow-motion* reps (whose
  absolute energy is low) from being split, while rests still separate demos.
- **Two-person gate** — a throw demonstration needs both tori and uke, so segments
  are filtered by their two-person coverage (drops single-person intro/close-up spans).
- **Self-similarity matrix + autocorrelation period** — a dependency-free,
  RepNet-style cross-check on the rep structure/count (soft, since reps vary in speed).

Energy sources (fusable): [`pose_motion_energy()`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.pose_motion_energy) (confidence-weighted total
keypoint speed; pose-only) and [`optical_flow_energy()`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.optical_flow_energy) (dense Farneback; pose-free).

### Functions

| [`estimate_period`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.estimate_period)(energy, fps, \*[, ...])         | Soft rep-period/count cross-check via autocorrelation of the energy signal.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`find_segments`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.find_segments)(energy, frame_indices, fps, \*)   | Turn a 1-D motion-energy signal into demonstration intervals via hysteresis.  |
| [`optical_flow_energy`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.optical_flow_energy)(video_path, \*[, ...])      | Per-frame mean dense optical-flow magnitude (Farneback), pose-free.           |
| [`pose_motion_energy`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.pose_motion_energy)(pose_seq, \*[, conf_thresh]) | Per-frame confidence-weighted total keypoint speed, summed over all people.   |
| [`segment_demonstrations`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.segment_demonstrations)(pose_seq, \*[, ...])     | Find demonstrations, annotate each with its two-person coverage, and gate.    |
| [`self_similarity_matrix`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.self_similarity_matrix)(pose_seq, \*[, ...])     | Frame×frame self-similarity on joint-angle features (for rep-structure viz).  |

### Classes

| [`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment)(index, start_s, end_s, start_frame, ...)   | One detected demonstration interval.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|

### *class* kodokan.segment.Segment(index, start_s, end_s, start_frame, end_frame, peak_activity, two_person_frac=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One detected demonstration interval.

### kodokan.segment.estimate_period(energy, fps, , smooth_sigma=4.0, min_period_s=1.5, max_period_s=10.0)

Soft rep-period/count cross-check via autocorrelation of the energy signal.

Returns `{period_s, count_est, strength}`. `strength` (0–1) is the
autocorrelation at the chosen lag — low values mean weak periodicity (expected
when reps vary a lot in speed), so treat the count as approximate.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.segment.find_segments(energy, frame_indices, fps, , smooth_sigma=4.0, low_quantile=0.25, high_quantile=0.5, min_duration_s=1.0, merge_gap_s=0.4)

Turn a 1-D motion-energy signal into demonstration intervals via hysteresis.

A demonstration starts when smoothed energy rises above the `high_quantile`
threshold and ends when it falls below the `low_quantile` threshold — so a
slow-motion dip in the middle of a rep does not split it, while the low-motion
rest between reps (below `low_quantile`) does separate them.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment)]

### kodokan.segment.optical_flow_energy(video_path, , frame_range=None, step=1, scale=0.4)

Per-frame mean dense optical-flow magnitude (Farneback), pose-free.

Returns `(energy, frame_indices)`. Frames are downscaled by `scale` for speed.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, `ndarray`]

### kodokan.segment.pose_motion_energy(pose_seq, , conf_thresh=0.2)

Per-frame confidence-weighted total keypoint speed, summed over all people.

Returns an array aligned to `pose_seq.frame_indices` (first sample is 0).
Robust to missing people/keypoints (NaNs are ignored).

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### kodokan.segment.segment_demonstrations(pose_seq, , video_path=None, use_optical_flow=False, min_two_person_frac=0.0, \*\*find_kwargs)

Find demonstrations, annotate each with its two-person coverage, and gate.

Uses pose motion energy by default (fuse optical flow with `use_optical_flow`).
Segments whose two-person coverage is below `min_two_person_frac` are dropped
(a throw demonstration needs both tori and uke), then re-indexed in time order.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment)]

### kodokan.segment.self_similarity_matrix(pose_seq, , person=None, max_frames=300)

Frame×frame self-similarity on joint-angle features (for rep-structure viz).

Returns `(sim, frame_indices_sub)`; repeated demonstrations appear as
off-diagonal bright blocks. Subsamples to `max_frames` for speed/readability.


# _autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md

# kodokan.store

dol-backed stores for the pipeline’s artifacts (the analysis SSOT).

Two dict-like stores keyed by `video_id`:

- [`pose_store()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.pose_store) — `video_id -> PoseSequence`, each persisted as a tidy/long
  **Parquet** file (columns `fidx, frame, t_sec, person, keypoint, x, y, conf`)
  with sequence metadata (fps, dims, backend, source_url, frame indices) carried in
  the Parquet schema metadata. Tidy/long Parquet is the analysis SSOT — columnar,
  compressed, and pandas/polars/DuckDB-native (research §6).
- [`segments_store()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.segments_store) — `video_id -> list[demo dicts]` as JSON.

[`load_all_tidy()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.load_all_tidy) concatenates every clip’s table (adding a `video_id` column)
into one DataFrame for cross-clip analysis.

### Functions

| [`check_sequence_integrity`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.check_sequence_integrity)(seq)                      | Integrity report for a single `PoseSequence` (via its tidy table).                                               |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_tidy_integrity`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.check_tidy_integrity)(df, \*[, width, height, ...]) | Row-level integrity checks on a tidy pose DataFrame.                                                             |
| [`load_all_tidy`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.load_all_tidy)([store])                             | Concatenate every clip's tidy table (with a `video_id` column) into one DataFrame.                               |
| [`parquet_bytes_to_sequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.parquet_bytes_to_sequence)(data)                    | Reconstruct a `PoseSequence` from Parquet bytes written above.                                                   |
| [`pose_store`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.pose_store)([directory])                            | A dict-like `{video_id: PoseSequence}` store backed by per-clip Parquet.                                         |
| [`segments_store`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.segments_store)([directory])                        | A dict-like `{video_id: <json>}` store for demo segments (and metadata).                                         |
| [`sequence_to_parquet_bytes`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.sequence_to_parquet_bytes)(seq)                     | Serialize a `PoseSequence` to Parquet bytes (tidy + schema metadata).                                            |
| [`sequence_to_tidy_df`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.sequence_to_tidy_df)(seq, \*[, video_id, ...])      | Convert a `PoseSequence` to a tidy/long DataFrame.                                                               |
| [`store_integrity_report`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.store_integrity_report)([store])                    | Run [`check_sequence_integrity()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.check_sequence_integrity) over every clip in a pose store. |

### kodokan.store.check_sequence_integrity(seq)

Integrity report for a single `PoseSequence` (via its tidy table).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.store.check_tidy_integrity(df, , width=None, height=None, oob_margin_frac=0.05)

Row-level integrity checks on a tidy pose DataFrame.

Returns counts of anomalies (all should be `0` for a clean store):

- `n_duplicate_rows`: rows sharing a `(fidx, person, keypoint)` key (each
  such triple must be unique per clip).
- `n_oob_xy`: keypoints falling outside the frame by more than
  `oob_margin_frac` of its size (only checked when `width`/`height` are
  given; a small margin is tolerated since limbs can extend just past frame).
- `n_bad_conf`: confidences outside `[0, 1]`.
- `n_nan_xy`: non-finite coordinates (occluded rows should have been dropped).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### kodokan.store.load_all_tidy(store=None)

Concatenate every clip’s tidy table (with a `video_id` column) into one DataFrame.

### kodokan.store.parquet_bytes_to_sequence(data)

Reconstruct a `PoseSequence` from Parquet bytes written above.

* **Return type:**
  [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence)

### kodokan.store.pose_store(directory=None)

A dict-like `{video_id: PoseSequence}` store backed by per-clip Parquet.

### kodokan.store.segments_store(directory=None)

A dict-like `{video_id: <json>}` store for demo segments (and metadata).

### kodokan.store.sequence_to_parquet_bytes(seq)

Serialize a `PoseSequence` to Parquet bytes (tidy + schema metadata).

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### kodokan.store.sequence_to_tidy_df(seq, , video_id=None, drop_missing=True)

Convert a `PoseSequence` to a tidy/long DataFrame.

One row per (frame, person, keypoint). `fidx` is the 0-based analyzed-frame
position; `frame` is the source frame index. A `video_id` column is added
when given (used by [`load_all_tidy()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.load_all_tidy)).

### kodokan.store.store_integrity_report(store=None)

Run [`check_sequence_integrity()`](_autosummary/kodokan.store.html.md#kodokan.store.check_sequence_integrity) over every clip in a pose store.

Returns `{video_id: report}`; a clip that fails to load records
`{"error": ...}` rather than aborting the whole sweep.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md

# kodokan.testmode

Technique test mode: perform the technique the system names, get scored (#5).

[`TechniqueTest`](_autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md#kodokan.testmode.TechniqueTest) draws a technique at random from a focus pool (all the
recognizer knows by default), names it, and grades the next performance on two
things: how confidently the recognizer sees the *target* in it, and, when a reference
for the target is given, how close it is to that reference (`kodokan.coach.coach()`,
with its advice). `TechniqueTest.push()` runs the same loop on a live pose stream.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from kodokan.recognizer import TechniqueRecognizer
>>> X = np.vstack([np.full((3, 4), c) + np.arange(3)[:, None] * 0.1 for c in (0.0, 3.0)])
>>> rec = TechniqueRecognizer(method="centroid").fit(X, ["o-goshi"] * 3 + ["uchi-mata"] * 3)
>>> test = TechniqueTest(rec, pool=["uchi-mata"], seed=1)
>>> test.next_prompt()
'uchi-mata'
>>> result = test.grade(np.full(4, 3.1))
>>> result.passed, result.score > 50
(True, True)
```

### Classes

| [`LiveTechniqueTest`](_autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md#kodokan.testmode.LiveTechniqueTest)(test, \*, fps[, featurize, ...])   | The test loop on a live stream: prompt, detect the throw, grade, prompt again.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TechniqueTest`](_autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md#kodokan.testmode.TechniqueTest)(recognizer, \*[, pool, ...])           | Prompt a random technique from a focus pool; grade the performance.              |
| [`TestResult`](_autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md#kodokan.testmode.TestResult)(target, recognition, ...)                 | The grade of one performance of the prompted technique.                          |

### *class* kodokan.testmode.LiveTechniqueTest(test, \*, fps, featurize=<function pooled_demo_descriptor>, angle_featurize=<function demo_features>, on_prompt=None, \*\*detector_kwargs)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The test loop on a live stream: prompt, detect the throw, grade, prompt again.

[`push()`](_autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md#kodokan.testmode.LiveTechniqueTest.push) takes one frame and returns `(segment, result)` for each throw that
closed with it; after each graded throw the next technique is drawn
(`prompt`). Detector options pass through.

A throw is graded once it has *closed* (`close_after_s` after it ends), so the
performer should wait for the next prompt before the next throw; any motion the
detector takes for a throw also uses up a prompt.

#### push(keypoints, frame_index=None)

Add one frame; grade each throw it closed and draw the next prompt.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/kodokan.segment.html.md#kodokan.segment.Segment), [`TestResult`](_autosummary/kodokan.testmode.html.md#kodokan.testmode.TestResult)]]

# _autosummary/kodokan.track.html.md

# kodokan.track

Stable tori/uke identity tracking (BoT-SORT / ByteTrack).

The plain [`estimate_poses()`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.estimate_poses) keeps the top-2 detections and
orders them left→right *per frame*, so the two slots swap whenever tori and uke
cross. This module instead runs a multi-object tracker (Ultralytics’ built-in
BoT-SORT by default — appearance ReID + camera-motion compensation) so each
person keeps a persistent `track_id` across frames; we then bind the two most
persistent tracks to fixed slots for the whole clip (ordered left→right by their
clip-average x), giving a stable identity that does not swap mid-throw.

Limitation: under the heavy mutual occlusion at a throw’s apex a track can
fragment (a person reappears with a new id). Top-2-by-presence captures the
dominant fragments; fragment-merging/ReID-stitching is a later refinement (see
`misc/docs/research-architecture.md` §4).

### Functions

| [`estimate_poses_tracked`](_autosummary/kodokan.track.html.md#kodokan.track.estimate_poses_tracked)(video_path, \*[, ...])   | Estimate per-frame keypoints with persistent tori/uke identity.                  |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`identity_swap_rate`](_autosummary/kodokan.track.html.md#kodokan.track.identity_swap_rate)(pose_seq)                    | Ground-truth-free track-identity discontinuity rate (a tracking-quality metric). |

### kodokan.track.estimate_poses_tracked(video_path, , n_persons=2, tracker='botsort.yaml', conf_thresh=0.3, max_gap_frac=0.15, stale_after=12, frame_step=1, frame_range=None, device='mps', model_name='yolo11n-pose.pt', source_url=None, progress=True)

Estimate per-frame keypoints with persistent tori/uke identity.

Returns a [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence) whose person slots are *stable*
across the clip (slot 0 = the track that is, on average, further left).

* **Parameters:**
  * **video_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Path to the clip.
  * **n_persons** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Number of stable identity slots to keep (2 for tori+uke).
  * **tracker** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Ultralytics tracker config (`"botsort.yaml"` or `"bytetrack.yaml"`).
  * **conf_thresh** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Minimum mean per-person confidence to count a detection.
  * **frame_step** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Analyze every n-th frame.
  * **frame_range** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional `(start, stop)` frame window.
  * **device** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Torch device (`"mps"`/`"cpu"`).
  * **model_name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – YOLO-pose weights (resolved under the data models dir).
  * **source_url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Provenance URL.
  * **progress** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Print progress.
* **Return type:**
  [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence)

### kodokan.track.identity_swap_rate(pose_seq)

Ground-truth-free track-identity discontinuity rate (a tracking-quality metric).

For each consecutive frame pair in which *all* person slots are present, we
solve the minimum-cost assignment between the two frames’ person centroids.
When the optimal assignment is not the identity (slot *i* → slot *i*), the
slots’ spatial positions are better explained by a **label swap** — a proxy
for a tori/uke identity swap that the review asked us to instrument. A stable
tracker trends toward `0`.

Returns `{n_pairs, n_swaps, swap_rate}`.

Caveat (honest): this also fires on a *genuine* physical crossing that the
tracker correctly follows through, so read `swap_rate` as a relative
diagnostic (compare trackers/clips), not an absolute error count.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/kodokan.viz.html.md

# kodokan.viz

Visualize a [`PoseSequence`](_autosummary/kodokan.pose.html.md#kodokan.pose.PoseSequence).

Two outputs, both requested by the project:

- [`render_skeleton_video()`](_autosummary/kodokan.viz.html.md#kodokan.viz.render_skeleton_video) — bake a shareable MP4 with the skeleton drawn
  either *on the original video* (overlay) or *on a blank canvas* (skeleton only).
- [`log_to_rerun()`](_autosummary/kodokan.viz.html.md#kodokan.viz.log_to_rerun) — log frames + 2D skeletons to a Rerun recording for
  interactive, scrubbable inspection (and side-by-side compare of two sequences).

Persons are drawn in distinct colors (slot 0 green, slot 1 magenta) so tori/uke
are visually separable.

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_PERSON_COLORS`](_autosummary/kodokan.viz.html.md#kodokan.viz.DEFAULT_PERSON_COLORS)   | BGR colors per person slot (green, magenta, cyan, yellow…).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`render_skeleton_video`](_autosummary/kodokan.viz.html.md#kodokan.viz.render_skeleton_video)(pose_seq, \*, out_path)     | Render skeletons to an MP4.                                                      |
